# Free tutorial: Your first Sigma rule

Turn a hunt into a detection rule that any SIEM can run.

The files for this seminar are in `~/case` (Linux) and `case/` (Python): `access.log`, `auth.log`, `eventlogs/Security.jsonl`, `shop2_access.log`.

## 1. The setting

This free tutorial is one step from **Seminar 2: Log search and detection as code**. Turn a hunt into a detection rule that any SIEM can run.

The evidence is in `~/case`. Read the README there if you want the whole story.

## 2. From hunt to rule: your first Sigma rule

A hunt you run once finds one attack. A **rule** finds the next one. Sigma is the open format for detection rules: one YAML file that converts to SPL, KQL and others.

Switch to the Windows case. On hr-pc07 Word started cmd.exe. The rule below fires on that, and on Excel or Outlook doing the same. Press **Test**, then **Convert with pySigma** to see the real converter's SPL.

- [ ] Test the rule: how many events match?
- [ ] Convert it with pySigma and compare with a search you would write by hand
- [ ] Why does PowerShell not match? (look at its parent)

> Hint: PowerShell's parent was cmd.exe, not Word. One rule per step of the chain, or a second rule for "cmd.exe starts PowerShell hidden".

```tool siem
{"q": "", "n": 1, "files": ["eventlogs/Security.jsonl"], "blank": ["q"], "a": {"q": "EventID=4688 | stats count by Computer"}}
```

```tool sigma
{"rule": "", "n": 1, "ls": true, "blank": ["rule"], "a": {"rule": "title: Office program starts a command shell
id: 5a1c7e10-0b8f-4a59-9a3e-2c1f00000001
status: experimental
description: Word, Excel or Outlook starting cmd.exe or PowerShell is how most macro malware begins.
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4688
    ParentProcessName|endswith:
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
    NewProcessName|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Office add-ins that call a script on purpose (rare; list them)
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
"}}
```

?> How many process-creation events (4688) are in Security.jsonl? :: sha256:e629fa6598d732768f7c726b4b621285f9c3b85303900aa912017db7617d8bdb
?> How many events does the Office-starts-a-shell rule match? :: sha256:6b86b273ff34fce19d6b804eff5a3f5747ada4eaa22f1d49c01e52ddb7875b4b

## 3. Where next

That was one step of **Seminar 2: Log search and detection as code**. The full seminar has the video, every step in three levels (walkthrough, practice and solo), a graded hand-in and a certificate.
